mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) over the past month consistently predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as stronger labor market conditions support consumer spending and corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months with a PAYEMS increase of at least 100k, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate above 4.0% signals a restrictive monetary policy that increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months with FEDFUNDS above 4.0%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and unemployment rate (FEDFUNDS rising and UNRATE rising) indicates a stagflationary environment that depresses equity returns, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months with both FEDFUNDS and UNRATE rising, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle economic expansions (characterized by GDPC1 growth above 2.5% and UNRATE below 4.5%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as valuations become stretched and the risk of a policy tightening increases, leading to negative forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months meeting the late-cycle expansion criteria (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% and UNRATE < 4.5%), or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A housing starts rate below 2000 thousand units (HOUST < 2000) signals weak demand for residential construction, which is a leading indicator of economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months with HOUST below 2000, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising trend in industrial production (INDPRO) over the past month indicates strengthening manufacturing activity, which supports corporate profits and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months with an INDPRO increase of at least 0.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In high-unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 5.5%), the Federal Reserve typically implements accommodative monetary policy, which boosts equity valuations and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of months with UNRATE above 5.5%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) indicates a broad-based economic slowdown, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of months with both HOUST and INDPRO declining, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.
